about: Tuned llama-server settings per model and route, applied by `1bit serve` (docs/recipes.md). A recipe never overrides a flag already on the backend's command line or a variable already set. Every recipe carries the measurement behind it; re-measure with tools/bench.py before changing one.

recipes.why: Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B (PrismML, Hadamard-folded qwen35) accepts 0.76 of 2-token MTP drafts vs 0.67 at 3: n2 wins prose / short / translation, n3-n4 win code by 4-8%.
recipes.measured: Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0 + mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0, HRX, performance mode, 2 servers, medians, code / prose / short / translation tok/s: n2 40.36 / 38.25 / 30.40 / 34.66, n3 41.65 / 36.81 / 27.18 / 33.18, n4 43.67 / 36.00 / 24.56 / 30.13 (2026-10-25).

recipes.why: DFlash2 proposes and verifies whole 8-token blocks, so a non-zero draft p-min discards blocks whose first tokens look unlikely and the loss lands on prose; 0 keeps every block whole. The flag is pinned here rather than left to llama-server's default, because the measurement below is what the recipe is for.
recipes.measured: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1bit serve --dflash with the Q8_0 drafter, greedy 256-token chats, medians of 3, performance mode, 2026-10-24: p-min 0 gives 56.6 / 30.8 / 20.6 tok/s on code / prose / short (acceptance 0.88 / 0.42 / 0.23); p-min 0.2, 0.4 and 0.6 cut prose to 22.5-23.3. The Q4_K drafter reaches 58.8 on code at p-min 0. Strict placement on: the drafter's graphs run on HRX in one graph split.

recipes.why: The model's own MTP head accepts about two thirds of its three drafts, and acceptance collapses past seven, so a longer verify batch costs more than the extra drafts return. The flag is llama-server's own (--spec-draft-n-max is what serve's --mtp-max 3 passes); capping there is what the measurement below is for. Do not raise it past 7.
recipes.measured: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL with its in-file MTP head, greedy 256-token chats, medians of 3, performance mode, 2026-10-24: --mtp-max 3 gives 32.6 / 26.9 / 28.0 tok/s on code / prose / short (12.1 / 12.1 / 12.5 without drafting). --mtp-max 7 --mtp-p-min 0 gives 37.9 / 22.4 / 22.4 and --mtp-max 15 33.6 / 14.9 / 13.5, with 0.17-0.60 acceptance past 8 drafts.

recipes.why: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's decode graph needs 66 distinct programs and the default count limit is 64, so at least one program is evicted and re-JITed for the whole run; one re-JIT costs about as much as four whole 36-layer GDN decode steps. The byte budget (8192 MiB) is not the binding constraint - the arenas sit at ~2.4 GiB - so raising only the count is the cheap half of this knob.
recipes.measured: Flash-Next UD-IQ3_XXS at -c 19456, 40-minute server run: 933 'trim_graph_programs: HRX graph program cache trimmed (1 of 66 programs, ... 64 max)' lines, and 779 in the pre-rebuild run of the same row, each trim evicting exactly one program and freeing ~6 MiB. On the same box (2026-11-04) a program that is not resident costs, measured as the first graph_compute of a fresh graph against the immediately following one: 40.9 / 46.0 / 42.7 ms for a 44 / 528 / 1584-node program (warm, flat in graph size), 110-136 ms first thing in a cold process, against steady p50 of 0.65 / 5.39 / 15.29 ms for those same graphs. On a 66-program-class model at cache 128 the same build logged 0 trims. NOT measured, and the reason this is a recipe rather than a default change: the tok/s effect at 18.8k, which needs the 76.33 GiB file with the box to itself (GTT >= 109 GiB measured at load). At the observed trim rate of ~1 per 10 decode steps the ceiling is ~4 ms/step; at 1 per step it would be ~41 ms/step.
